planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in warm, humus-rich, well-drained soil after all frost danger has passed, in a sheltered site with morning sun and afternoon shade in hotter climates.

directions: Java glorybower is a fast-growing tropical shrub from Southeast Asia prized for its large, felted, heart-shaped leaves and showy upright pyramidal clusters of brilliant orange-scarlet flowers held above the foliage nearly year-round in frost-free climates. It thrives in moist but well-drained, fertile soil and benefits from a partial-shade site in hot summer regions, though it flowers most heavily with several hours of direct morning sun. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and cut back hard after flowering flushes to maintain a compact, floriferous habit, since the shrub can become leggy if left unpruned. In marginal zone 9 sites it usually dies back to the ground in winter but resprouts readily from the roots once soil warms, and it is a strong hummingbird and butterfly attractant wherever it is grown.
sources: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Species Profile
